cap: The thyroid nodule work-up as a decision path: serum TSH comes first; a low TSH leads to scintigraphy, where a hot nodule is rarely malignant, while a normal or high TSH leads to ultrasound and fine-needle aspiration of suspicious nodules. Follicular neoplasms need histology because only the capsule shows invasion.
teach: Read the figure top to bottom. The branch point is the TSH: function lowers cancer risk, so a suppressed TSH sends the patient to a scan rather than a needle. A cold nodule rejoins the ultrasound path. Fine-needle aspiration sorts cells into benign, follicular neoplasm or malignant, and only the follicular group needs molecular testing or lobectomy to settle the diagnosis.
